correctness.rationale: Invert the natural-curvature tridiagonal matrix exactly, derive checkerboard signed cardinal tails and their two finite-boundary negative masses. Reflection reduces all-grid mass to two inequalities. The listed nonnegative tensor Bernstein coefficients certify both for all X,Y in [0,1], establishing the global sharp bound without numerical exhaustion. A central long-grid limit proves sharpness and strict finite deficiency; extremizing positive nodal weights produces the iff contrast. Separate exact checker reproduces certificate and 315 finite cardinal identities. Risks: future independent inspection of Green-tail sign algebra; no independent audit performed.

originality.rationale: The infinite-cardinal norm is explicitly known from Powell as reported by Beatson–Chacko, and is not claimed new; their finite natural Method E data are numerical. The finding is the all-n *finite natural-endpoint* inequality, its strict nonattainment, and a sharp all-grid positive-nodal-ratio classification using a bivariate Bernstein certificate. Related fixed-knot, monotone-data, and local-spline results do not imply the claimed theorem on the inspected evidence. Historical priority may be affected by undiscovered finite-boundary theorems.

value.rationale: An exact universal data-contrast test guarantees that unchanged natural cubic interpolation never leaves the positive cone for all equidistant grid sizes; a finite-grid counterexample is constructed above the sharp threshold. The natural shape-preservation problem and global finite-boundary control are motivated independently of any small-grid computation; practical data positivity makes the precise threshold useful. Does not claim general irregular meshes or accuracy improvements.
